title: Egg omelet with meat and tomatoes, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Egg omelet with meat and tomatoes, no added fat is a dish made from eggs, lean meat (usually turkey or chicken) and fresh tomatoes, cooked without oil or other fats. It is prepared on a dry pan or in a microwave, preserving most nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are a complete protein source containing all essential amino acids.
Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after heating.
Cooking without added fat reduces the calorie content by about 30 % compared with a traditional omelet.
Lean meat adds extra protein and iron without increasing saturated fat.
The dish can be quickly prepared in a microwave, saving time and energy.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs and lean meat provide complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and minerals
items.content: Tomatoes supply vitamin C and potassium, while eggs provide vitamin D, B12 and selenium.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes the dish suitable for low‑saturated‑fat diets.

items.title: Supports satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fiber from tomatoes helps keep you full longer.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and lutein from eggs help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to eggs and should avoid the dish.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Eggs should be fully cooked to eliminate the risk of salmonella.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If processed meat with added salt is used, monitor overall sodium intake.

items.title: Portion size
items.content: Large portions can increase total calories despite the lack of added fat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the omelet hot, garnished with fresh herbs. It is convenient for a lunch box and pairs well with whole‑grain bread or a vegetable salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked omelet in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in a microwave or dry pan without adding fat.
